structured.answer: I'd open an account at פסגות and buy the ילין לפידות S&P 500 fund. The page calls it "הזוג הזול ביותר לתוכנית שלכם": 86,492 ₪ after 10 years, compared with 84,184 for the אינטראקטיב option it had pre-selected for me. But I'm not sure that's right, and the page never showed it with my own 30,000.

stuck.why: The page pre-selected אינטראקטיב ישראל (MEXEM LTD) as 'הבחירה שלכם', a name I don't know. I never chose it, so I didn't know which box was the recommendation.

פסגות is named in the 'cheapest pair', but in the account list its row says 'אין נתון' and the 86,492 is labelled as coming from a 'קרן אחרת'. That left me unsure whether פסגות really is the cheapest.
They were set to 10,000 / 500 / 10 years / 7%, not my 30,000, so I never saw my own result.
At 7% for 10 years I expected about 70% more. 84k felt low, and I didn't understand the 'בכסף של היום' / after-tax explanation.
Dozens of near-identical funds with coloured tags. Too many to choose from, and I got bored there.

findings.what: An unknown broker is pre-selected as 'הבחירה שלכם', and its 84,184 is the first big number you see, even though I never chose it
The cheapest pair names פסגות, but פסגות's row in the account list shows 'אין נתון' with a figure for a 'קרן אחרת'. Confusing.
findings.where: Screen 1 top-left box vs screen 3 account list

findings.what: Too many near-identical funds covered in jargon tags; I'd give up there
Default amounts aren't mine, so I couldn't see my own result
84k from 70k at 7% over 10 years looks low, and the reason isn't clear
Negative percentages on funds look scary and aren't explained up front
